Slow Habits and Careful Looking

By Jordan Ellis, published March 3

Early Habits

Tomato seedlings need steady warmth before they can be moved outdoors. A thin layer of compost keeps the soil moist through dry weeks.

Careful pruning in late winter encourages stronger growth in spring. Marigolds planted between the rows help to discourage some common pests. Rainwater collected in a barrel is gentler on young roots than tap water.

Most herbs prefer a sunny spot and soil that drains quickly. The old apple tree still produces a heavy crop every second year. Tomato seedlings need steady warmth before they can be moved outdoors. A thin layer of compost keeps the soil moist through dry weeks.

A thin layer of compost keeps the soil moist through dry weeks. Bees visit the lavender hedge from mid morning until the shade returns.

Reading the Sky

The Moon is slowly drifting away from the Earth by a few centimetres each year. Comets grow bright tails only when they approach the warmth of the Sun. Light from the nearest star takes more than four years to reach us.

Dark skies far from cities make faint galaxies much easier to see. The planet Jupiter has more than seventy known moons. On a clear night, the faint band of the Milky Way stretches across the sky. Astronomers measure distances to nearby stars using a method called parallax.

Astronomers measure distances to nearby stars using a method called parallax. A small telescope reveals the rings of Saturn as a delicate golden line.

Comets grow bright tails only when they approach the warmth of the Sun. Light from the nearest star takes more than four years to reach us. Dark skies far from cities make faint galaxies much easier to see.

Patience is the quiet skill behind every careful observation.

Crossing the Water

The earliest bridges were simple logs laid across narrow streams. Roman engineers perfected the stone arch, and many of their spans still carry traffic. Suspension bridges hang their decks from long cables anchored at both ends. Iron and later steel allowed builders to cross far wider rivers than before.

Iron and later steel allowed builders to cross far wider rivers than before. A well designed truss spreads the load through many small triangles.

Maintenance crews inspect cables and bearings on a regular schedule. Wooden covered bridges were roofed to protect the timber from rain and snow. The earliest bridges were simple logs laid across narrow streams.

Roman engineers perfected the stone arch, and many of their spans still carry traffic. Suspension bridges hang their decks from long cables anchored at both ends. Iron and later steel allowed builders to cross far wider rivers than before. A well designed truss spreads the load through many small triangles.

  • Inspect the foundations after heavy rain.
  • Check every cable for signs of wear.
  • Keep a written record of each repair.

A Cup in the Morning

Water that is just below boiling extracts the pleasant flavours without bitterness. Freshly roasted beans are usually best within a few weeks.

Cold brew is steeped for many hours and tastes smooth and sweet. Coffee plants grow best on high slopes with mild temperatures and steady rain. After harvest, the ripe cherries are dried or washed to remove the fruit.

Roasting changes the colour, aroma and flavour of the green beans. A coarse grind suits a plunger pot, while a fine grind suits a small espresso machine. Water that is just below boiling extracts the pleasant flavours without bitterness. Freshly roasted beans are usually best within a few weeks.

Freshly roasted beans are usually best within a few weeks. Many cafes now list the farm or cooperative that grew their beans.
